rationale: This sample is a small, string-centric Shootout benchmark (strcat) with no large function inventory, so cheap low-risk passes should dominate: SUB and SPLIT get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with high CorrectnessRisk and low effective cost sensitivity, since arithmetic obfuscation and block splitting add strong resistance to a character-loop-heavy workload at negligible overhead. FLA keeps high SecurityGain because flattening the string-processing loops yields the biggest reversal deterrent, but its RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are held near 0.5 so the selector avoids flattening hot inner loops where per-iteration dispatch would be costly; BCF is similarly dampened (cost weights ~0.4) because bogus-clique duplication inflates an already branch-dense string loop without proportional benefit. IBR and ICALL sit in the middle: useful for breaking static branch/call recovery on this small binary, but throttled because indirect dispatch overhead lands directly in the character-copy hot path. IGV is weighted lowest, as a Shootout-style benchmark has few globals and indirect-global lowering adds correctness risk and TableGen-style lookup cost with little to protect.
